I think this is more of a case of people recognizing the economy is bad shape for society outside of the wealthy - wages are stagnant to declining, the quality of jobs available is on the decline, and even people with advanced degrees are having trouble finding meaningful employment. So they look for a cause and buy into it being illegal immigration.

While illegal immigrants are certainly taking up some positions that citizens could be working it's in no way the source of the problem. The source of the problem is that worker productivity in the US has skyrocketed. Here is a graph of worker productivity it from the St Louis Fed. One employee of today is producing as much as several employees of years past. The problem with this is that many of today's employers are not constrained on supply. They can and do produce enough of whatever product they offer to meet demand. So what happens when worker productivity doubles? No, they don't double their production. Instead they fire half their employees and keep producing the exact same amount but with more profit for themselves.

As you can see from the graph we're starting to seeing accelerating growth in worker productivity. The onset of automation is going to send productivity per [human] worker through the roof to levels we've never seen before. This is the giant pink elephant nobody wants to touch because fixing it isn't going to require a bandaid here and there but a complete rethinking of our entire economic system. When the number of employees required for the operation of all businesses within a society drops far below the working population of that country - what happens? Even something as blunt as decreasing the population does nothing. This scales with population. As population decreases the necessary output to meet demand falls in proportion which in turn means a need for fewer employees.

Although it's an important factor, Increases in worker productivity isn't the sole cause of the problem.

Our entire economic system is based on assumptions about constant growth, economists treat it like the Holy Grail. Economists talk about GDP and economic growth, worrying if the growth drops below a certain rate. Inflation is considered normal, and while runaway inflation must be prevented (see Zimbabwe) the idea of 0% inflation or negative inflation (deflation) is unthinkable.

Over the last 50 years women have been urged to enter the workforce, massively increasing the number of workers, earning and spending money, boosting economic growth. But that's really run it's course, pretty much all the women that can work, are working. Certainly there are still programs pushing for more childcare to get more women working, but the boost to the economy from women is pretty much over. But one of the unexpected (??) consequences of getting so many women to work full time has been a substantial drop in the birthrate.

The birthrate for non-immigrant families is below replacement levels. A shrinking population would almost certainly result in a shrinking economy, automation and increased worker productivity can only do so much. The idea of accepting a shrinking economy is simply unthinkable to most economists, investors assume their investments will grow, people assume banks will pay them interest, property owners assume their property will increase in value, ongoing negative economic growth would basically break the economy as we know it.

From an economic point of view, one way to offset the reduced birthrate is large scale immigration, increasing the number of people, increases the size of the economy. And the idea of the economy not continuing to increase terrifies a lot of people, especially those who've done really well from the current system..

Which is pretty much why so many of the ultra wealthy are pro-immigration. (illegal or otherwise).
